honor of the man of Paul's Valley came to the Chickasaw Nation. He was the first settler there, coming to the Mississippi, where he removed to the Indian Territory in the '70's. A later date he removed to Mississippi, where he married a woman whose maiden name was Lucy White, of the Chickasaw tribe, and with her people came to the Indian Territory in the '70's. A man of ninety years of age. He was a prominent farmer and stock-dealer, and one of the nation's most valued citizens of the nation until his death, which occurred at Tishomingo, Oklahoma.

His first wife was Lucy White, of the Chickasaw Nation. He later married Lucy White, of the Chickasaw tribe. He is now ninety years old, is still living and is a prominent farmer and stock-dealer and is one of the most valued citizens of the nation.

He then came to the Indian Territory and became one of the prominent and influential men of the country and its community. He was influential in molding public thought and action in the territory. He served both in the legislature and senate. He served both in the legislature and senate. His second wife was Sarah Lambert, a native Englishman, of Iowa, and they have three children. Charles J. Johnson, was born in 1868 at Sherman, Texas.

He then married a woman and has molded public thought. He was influential in molding the public policy. At one time he acted as Senator at the senate. He was born in 1868 at Sherman, Texas. His second wife was Sarah Lambert, a native English-woman, of Iowa, and they have three children, two of whom are living: Smith, whose name is now living, and Will, and they now hold many positions in the college. He has also served as a member of the senate. At one time he acted as senator at the senate. He has also served as a member of the Senate at the senate.
